etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English manifest, manifeste, from Latin manifestus, manufestus (“palpable, manifest”), from manus (“hand”) + *infestus, participle of *infendō (“strike”) (from the root of dēfendō, offendō, etc.), or from Proto-Indo-European *dʰers-. Doublet of manifesto.

definitions.definition: Evident to the senses, especially to the sight; apparent; distinctly perceived.

quote.citation: 2017 October 27, Alex McLevy, “Making a Killing: The Brief Life and Bloody Death of the Post-Scream Slasher Revival”, in The A.V. Club‎[1], archived from the original on 5 March 2018:
quote.text: It re-envisioned Freddy Krueger in the “real world,” where the nightmare-dwelling being is made manifest in our reality, one where Freddy actor Robert Englund and original Nightmare On Elm Street star Heather Langenkamp play themselves, as does [Wes] Craven himself.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Hebrews 4:13:
quote.text: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight […]

definitions.definition: Obvious to the understanding; apparent to the mind; easily apprehensible; plain; not obscure or hidden.

quote.citation: 1700, [John] Dryden, “Palamon and Arcite: Or, The Knight’s Tale. In Three Books.”, in Fables Ancient and Modern; […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC, book II, page 47:
quote.text: Caliſtho there ſtood manifeſt of Shame, / And turn’d a Bear, the Northern Star became […]

definitions.definition: A list or invoice of the passengers or goods being carried by a commercial vehicle or ship.
(computing) A file containing metadata describing other files.
(obsolete) A public declaration; an open statement; a manifesto.

quote.citation: 1700, [John] Dryden, “Homer’s Ilias”, in Fables Ancient and Modern; […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC, book I, pages 206–7:
quote.text: But you, authentick Witneſſes I bring, / Before the gods, and your ungrateful King, / Of this my Manifeſt : That never more / This Hand ſhall combate on the crooked Shore : / No, let the Grecian Powers oppreſs’d in Fight, / Unpity’d periſh in their Tyrants fight.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To show plainly; to make to appear distinctly, usually to the mind; to put beyond question or doubt; to display; to exhibit.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Othello, the Moore of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene ii], page 312, column 1:
quote.text: My Parts, my Title, and my perfect Soule / Shall manifeſt me rightly.

quote.citation: 1988, Dennis Marcellino, Sweeping it under the drug, page 123:
quote.text: And usually this manifests as them trying to prove their parent's criticism's and belittlings wrong.

quote.citation: 2012 April 19, Josh Halliday, “Free speech haven or lawless cesspool – can the internet be civilised?”, in The Guardian‎[2]:
quote.text: Other global taboos, such as sex and suicide, manifest themselves widely online, with websites offering suicide guides and Hot XXX Action seconds away at the click of a button. The UK government will come under pressure to block access to pornographic websites this year when a committee of MPs publishes its report on protecting children online.

quote.citation: 2012, Justin D. Yeakel et al., “Stable isotopes, functional morphology, and human evolution: a model of consilience”, in arXiv‎[3]:
quote.text: Molar enamel thickness is a morphological trait that differentiates African apes from hominins, being manifested most dramatically in the megadont hominins (Paranthropus spp.) with hyperthick enamel.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To become manifest; to be revealed.
(transitive, initially occult, now slang) To will something to exist.

quote.citation: 1982, Shakti Gawain, The Creative Visualization Workbook‎[4]:
quote.text: The process of creating your treasure map is a powerful step toward manifesting your goal. Now just spend a few minutes each day looking at it […]

quote.citation: 2014, Adrian Calabrese, How to Get Everything You Ever Wanted: Complete Guide to Using Your Psychic Common Sense‎[5]:
quote.text: Undaunted by poverty, I decided to manifest a new car.

quote.citation: 2021, Kyle Buchanan, “Dominique Fishback Gave Her Heart to ‘Judas and the Black Messiah’”, in The New York Times‎[6]:
quote.text: To Fishback, the project is a perfect fit. “I’ve been manifesting a romance role for a really long time,” she said,

definitions.definition: (transitive) To exhibit the manifests or prepared invoices of; to declare at the customhouse.
